title: Choir and Salt
premise: Dominic Quintana, a memory-thief who keeps the ledgers of the Saltwork Guild—a syndicate that trades in impossible commodities—has survived by being forgettable and forgetting. When a dying courier presses a map of the court beneath Mount Verity into his hands, Dominic learns the courier's soul was sold there as collateral, and that his own stolen childhood memories were the payment that sealed the deal years ago. To reclaim both souls, he must infiltrate the court, outwit its memory-devouring Regent, and betray the guild that made him. In the end, Dominic chooses to return every memory he has ever stolen—including his own—dissolving his power and his past, but gaining at last a self he can call home.
about_author: Mara Nakamura is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing other people's letters before turning to fiction. Raised between a coastal fishing town and a mountain monastery, she writes about the weight of things we carry and the ones we leave behind.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Sins
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. He balances the guild's books by candlelight, cataloguing traded years, first kisses, and a duchess's grief. We learn he keeps one memory of his own locked away—a door he never opens. Beat: quiet competence masking loneliness; the reader sees a man who has made himself a stranger to himself.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Salt Door
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A bleeding courier staggers into the guild's back room and dies pressing a wax-sealed map into Dominic's hands, whispering 'the Regent keeps what's mine.' Guild enforcers arrive minutes behind. Beat: fear and the first crack in Dominic's invisibility; he hides the map in the one place no thief would look—inside a memory he steals from himself.

chapters.title: What the Guild Buys
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, with a flashback in the Guildmaster Odile's voice. He tours the guild's vault of bottled memories, learning the courier's soul was sold as collateral to the court beneath Mount Verity—and that the purchase price, years ago, was paid in a boy's childhood. His childhood. Beat: vertigo; the ledger turns on its keeper.

chapters.title: The Weight of a Borrowed Name
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Odile suspects him and assigns a charming enforcer, Sera Voss, to shadow him. Their cat-and-mouse through the harbor market reveals she trades in loyalty, not memory, and she's watching for betrayal. Beat: wary attraction and mutual deception; Dominic realizes the map makes him a target for everyone.

chapters.title: The Door He Never Opens
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, dreamlike. Desperate to decode the map, he finally unlocks his own hidden memory and finds a mountain, a singing, and his mother's face—then the memory tears, cut out by a professional hand. Beat: grief for a self he never got to have; the map's markings match his dream exactly.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Daughter
chapters.summary: New POV: Wren, the dead courier's daughter, finds Dominic and demands the map—or revenge. She reveals the court beneath the mountain buys souls to sing the Regent's mountain stable, and her father went to buy hers back. Beat: reluctant alliance; Dominic, who trusts no one, chooses to trust someone anyway.

chapters.title: Salt and Ash
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Odile confronts him with evidence of theft and offers a bargain: deliver the map to the court on the guild's behalf, and she'll erase the trail leading to him. He realizes she intends to trade his soul as well. Beat: betrayal crystallizes; he agrees while planning to betray her first.

chapters.title: The Road Under the World
chapters.summary: Dominic and Wren's POV, alternating. They descend the old salt-miners' road, navigating a landscape where forgotten memories pool like water and can be drunk. Dominic tastes a stranger's wedding day; Wren nearly drowns in her father's last hours. Beat: intimacy through shared vulnerability; the mountain begins to hum.

chapters.title: The Singing Stone
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. They reach the mountain's throat, where the stone itself remembers everything and sings it back. The song shows Wren her father's final act—he traded his own soul to buy passage for hers. Beat: sorrow and resolve; Wren stops wanting the map and starts wanting the Regent's head.

chapters.title: Court of Kept Things
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. They enter the court beneath the mountain: a cathedral of shelves where souls are filed like documents, tended by the Hollow, courtiers who sold their names for rank. Dominic's thief's instincts read the place as a vault. Beat: awe and horror; he spots his own childhood on a shelf, labeled in Odile's hand.

chapters.title: The Regent's Hospitality
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The Regent—courteous, ancient, and hollow-eyed—receives them, revealing she knows exactly what Dominic is: a thief who steals memories, the perfect instrument. She offers him Wren's soul in exchange for the map and one more theft. Beat: temptation; the price is the memory of Wren herself.

chapters.title: Terms of Trade
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, night in the guest cells. He and Wren argue: take the deal and forget her, or refuse and likely die. Sera Voss arrives with Odile's delegation, and Dominic learns Odile sold the guild's entire vault to the Regent to buy herself immortality. Beat: stakes sharpen; every ally has a price, and Dominic must decide what his is.

chapters.title: The Thief's Grammar
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Studying the court's filing system, he discovers souls can be moved by ledger-entry—a theft of paperwork, his oldest skill. He begins forging entries with Wren as accomplice, stealing back her father's soul first. Beat: hope and momentum; the heist structure assembles, but each forgery alerts the Regent.

chapters.title: What Odile Sold
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Ordered to retrieve the map, Sera instead finds Odile's contract and learns her own loyalty was purchased—her devotion is a bottled memory the guild installed. Shaken, she defects to Dominic, bringing the guild's vault keys. Beat: a mirror to Dominic's arc; another stolen self choosing to steal herself back.

chapters.title: The Regent's Hunger
chapters.summary: Regent's POV, rare and chilling. She was the mountain's first singer, who ate her own memories to gain power and now must be fed souls to remember how to rule. She senses the forgeries and begins unspooling the court's stored memories to hunt the thieves. Beat: dread; the antagonist becomes pitiable and more dangerous for it.

chapters.title: Ledger of the Damned
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The heist: Dominic, Wren, and Sera forge a mass transfer, emptying the court's shelves into a single ledger. The Hollow catch them mid-entry; Sera holds the door at terrible cost, her purchased loyalty burning out of her. Beat: triumph curdling into sacrifice; the ledger is won, Sera is captured.

chapters.title: The Bargain Reversed
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The Regent offers his final trade: Sera and Wren's souls for his own stolen childhood—the original payment, still sealed in her vault. He accepts, walking into the vault alone. Beat: apparent surrender; Dominic hands over the map, and the Regent begins to open his childhood like a letter.

chapters.title: The Memory of a Boy
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, inside the opened memory. He relives his seventh year: his mother singing, the guild's agents, the sale. But the memory contains what no one knew—his mother was the Regent's own daughter, and the Regent ate her. Beat: revelation; Dominic's theft and the Regent's hunger share one root, and his grief becomes a weapon.

chapters.title: The Unmaking Song
chapters.summary: Dominic, Wren, and freed souls' POV, converging. Dominic sings his mother's song into the court's shelves, and every stored soul remembers itself; the Hollow wake and remember their names. The Regent, flooded with memories she cannot digest, begins to come apart. Beat: climax; the mountain shakes, shelves collapse, and Dominic holds the whole court's memory in his hands.

chapters.title: Everything He Ever Stole
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. To end the Regent without becoming her, Dominic must pour every memory he carries—hers, the court's, his own—back into the world. He releases them all, emptying himself to a blank page. Beat: climax's cost; the Regent dissolves into the mountain, and Dominic stands in the rubble remembering nothing, not even why he's crying.

chapters.title: A Blank Page
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren keeps the ledger and reads it to the memory-less Dominic daily—his name, his mother's song, the story of what he gave away. Sera, freed, rebuilds the guild as a house of return rather than theft. Beat: tenderness after ruin; identity rebuilt from the outside in, by the people who stayed.

chapters.title: Choir and Salt
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, final chapter. A year later, Dominic cannot remember his past but has begun making new memories—salt on his lips, Wren's voice, a ledger he keeps of small kindnesses instead of sins. On the mountain, the freed souls' choir still sings, and he hums along without knowing why. Beat: resolution; belonging found not in what was kept, but in what was given.
